Apply warm purple hero background with white text and orange solid primary CTA; secondary CTA as outlined/ghost. Keep headline sizing aligned to long-form rule for 16+ words. Add a compact logos-first trust band directly in hero using 100,000+ businesses proof.

White background, 1px border cards, 24px padding, 2-column grid on desktop because there are 4 features.

sections.variantHint: 4-card grid with section header and enterprise-oriented copy

figmaExecutionNotes: Keep the build strictly aligned to the provided content; do not add unsupported sections such as pricing, testimonials, forms, or news.
Use a mobile adaptation where the hero stacks vertically with CTAs full-width and stacked, trust bar remains compact, and all feature grids collapse to a single column.
Avoid oversized image placeholders and avoid strip-style placeholders; use dense card layouts so no section feels underfilled.
Use Techjockey default typography tokens: Plus Jakarta Sans for headings and Inter for body, with warm collaboration palette and orange CTA accent.
Ensure logo/customer-count trust is visually dominant across hero and trust sections, since proof strategy prioritizes logos most.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected asymmetrical hero: keep the copy on the right in a strong editorial stack, while the left side features a layered enterprise dashboard mockup with floating app chips for Mail, Cliq, Writer, Meetings, and WorkDrive. Add a slim logo-first trust band directly beneath the subheadline, and include one compact stat pill row to reinforce 100,000+ businesses. Brand red must drive both CTAs and key highlights. The hero should feel like a clean operational control center, not a marketing illustration. Use a soft mesh gradient with subtle grid lines and a few red orbital accents for depth. Typography must be dramatic: H1 at 64px+ and H2 at 40px+, with crisp enterprise spacing and premium soft-shadow cards.

repetitionBreakers: Split hero with product visual right and continuity-driven ad-match messaging left
Logo-first trust bar immediately after hero to anchor enterprise credibility
How-it-works section uses a compact 3-step horizontal timeline instead of cards
Feature blocks alternate between spotlight-plus-grid and split-panel visuals to avoid repeated patterns
Testimonials use a carousel rather than a grid because there are 5 quotes
Pricing is isolated in a centered highlighted card to reset rhythm before the final CTA
Final form section is intentionally simpler and more conversion-led than earlier sections
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprises | Unified Email and Collaboration Suite
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace for enterprises with unified email, chat, documents, meetings, and secure collaboration. See trusted logos, key features, pricing, and get started.

sections.backgroundTreatment: light split hero with white-to-slate wash and subtle dashboard-grid texture
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep the headline enterprise-clear and continuity-matched to the ad: Zoho Workplace as an all-in-one email and collaboration suite for enterprises. Use a product dashboard mockup on the right with floating app chips for Mail, Cliq, Writer, Meetings, and WorkDrive. Include a compact supporting-benefits row beneath the CTA. CTA remains only 'Get started' in solid Zoho red and visually dominant.

Place trust immediately after the hero. Show 3-6 recognizable customer logos in a slim horizontal band, with the customer-count badge secondary and smaller. If logo availability is limited, convert to a metric strip, but keep the visual light and fast-scanning. This section should feel like an enterprise credibility checkpoint rather than a testimonial block.

This section should combine the required how-it-works flow with the strongest feature story, rather than using a generic SaaS grid. First panel: a 3-step, under-60-seconds workflow explaining setup, collaboration, and daily use. Second panel: a spotlight on the core click-driving feature, All-in-One Unified Workspace, with a preview panel showing email, chat, docs, and meetings in one interface. Third panel: a tight supporting panel for real-time collaboration and AI productivity. Keep the rhythm alternating between text-led and visual-led blocks so adjacent sections never feel identical.

Use a compact enterprise-trust explanation block only if the content is present; in this blueprint, keep it minimal because the primary trust strategy is logos-first. Since the source content has whyTechjockey excluded, this section should be omitted or replaced with a slim reassurance strip only if required by the page system. Do not let it interrupt the conversion rhythm.

Present one highlighted enterprise pricing card with included services and support benefits. Keep the layout restrained and legible, with the red CTA button as the only action. This section should feel practical and procurement-friendly rather than salesy.

Because there are 5 testimonials, use a carousel. Make it quote-first with author, role, and company hierarchy. The carousel should feel credible and operational, not promotional. Keep card surfaces clean with subtle shadow and short quote truncation for scanability.

Final conversion block should be a simplified centered card with strong supporting copy and one action only: Get started. Keep the field set minimal if used at all. Mobile CTA must be full-width. This is the final reassurance-and-action moment, so the layout should be quieter than the hero but more urgent than the middle sections.

No media/news content is available, so do not force a news block. If the page system requires this slot, use it as an optional secondary logo or compliance strip. Keep it visually lightweight and non-competing.

blueprint.designPersonality: A crisp, enterprise productivity system with strong brand-red accents, white space discipline, logos-first trust hierarchy, and dashboard-style components that make Zoho Workplace feel reliable, organized, and easy to adopt.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a polished Zoho Workplace-style dashboard mockup, floating collaboration chips for Mail, Cliq, Writer, Meetings, and WorkDrive, plus a clean trust strip of customer logos as the dominant proof element. The visual should feel like an enterprise suite overview rather than a marketing illustration. Add compact stat pills and app icons, but keep the layout spacious only around the hero visual and dense in feature sections.
blueprint.primaryGoal: Drive enterprise evaluation and demo-start intent for Zoho Workplace by matching the ad message, proving trust early, and moving visitors toward a single Get started action.
blueprint.narrativeMode: continuity-first enterprise story: what it is, how it works, why it is trusted, what features matter most, then a final conversion prompt

Learn from the brrand

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is medium length and needs enough scale to feel enterprise-grade while staying balanced on a split layout.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top hero with brand/logo at the upper left, followed by a centered or left-aligned headline block. Uses a bold H1, a short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefits list with tick icons. Visual hierarchy is strong and conversion-focused, with CTA emphasis implied in the hero/form pairing rather than a single large hero button.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Long-form single-page sales layout. Starts with a prominent hero, then immediately transitions into a lead-capture form card, followed by stacked information sections with repeating headline + description + feature grid patterns. Sections are arranged vertically with clear separation and consistent internal spacing.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primary card treatment is functional rather than decorative: white/light card surfaces, simple borders or shadow separation, rounded corners, and dense form/content blocks. Feature cards appear structured and grid-based, with minimal ornamentation and strong text-first layout.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Conversion-oriented dual-CTA pattern in the hero context, paired with form-first lead capture. Primary CTA is stronger and action-driven; secondary CTA acts as a lower-friction alternative. CTAs are placed near the top and repeated through the funnel rather than distributed heavily across the page.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the referenced structure. The layout favors inquiry/lead-gen over self-serve pricing.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not represented in the provided reference structure. Likely minimal or standard utility footer rather than a content-heavy closing band.
spacingScale: medium vertical spacing between content rows
large section gaps between major blocks
container-based centered content with generous side padding
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-first header treatment with limited hero imagery visible in the extracted structure. The page leans more on typography and iconography than large product visuals. Media, where present, supports trust and recognition rather than feature demonstration.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Repeating section formula: small label/kicker, headline, short summary, then a feature grid. Features are presented as concise title + description units, optimized for scanning. Content appears modular and scalable for multiple feature categories.
referenceMap.formPattern: Prominent lead form placed immediately after the hero. Uses a boxed card layout, likely with multiple hidden tracking fields, suggesting a conversion-optimized, CRM-integrated form workflow. Form is positioned as a central action step rather than an isolated contact page.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Light-touch motion only, with carousel-based slide behavior as the primary interaction. No evidence of elaborate reveal, parallax, or animated metric systems.
designNotes: The page is optimized for enterprise lead generation, not exploratory browsing.
Structure emphasizes immediate value proposition, trust cues, and fast conversion.
Content hierarchy is straightforward and scan-friendly, with repeated headline-supporting copy-feature patterns.
Use modular sections that can scale to long-form product messaging without feeling visually noisy.
Favor strong typography, restrained visuals, and clear conversion paths over decorative UI.

mustHaveMoments: Prominent logo/trust strip immediately above or adjacent to the hero content
Clear enterprise-oriented hero message with a compact benefit list
Fast-follow lead capture or trial CTA reinforced within the first screen
Feature sections with tightly grouped cards and minimal vertical waste
Pricing/cart section clearly visible and not omitted
Testimonials placed after feature proof to reinforce purchase confidence
Integration/apps section to validate ecosystem fit for enterprise buyers
avoidPatterns: Large empty gaps around feature imagery or cards
Misaligned visuals that leave unused whitespace
Generic strip-heavy layouts that feel repetitive
Hero copy that does not exactly match the provided content
Replacing provided content with paraphrased or missing sections
Burying logo trust signals below the fold
Using decorative visuals that do not support enterprise credibility
designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Workplace for enterprises is a solution-aware, conversion-focused page where visitors need fast validation rather than education from scratch. Since the strongest trust signal is logos, the page should lead with proof first, then product clarity. A split hero works best because it can hold a strong message on one side and proof/CTA support on the other without wasting space. Dense but well-structured sections suit the long-form content volume and prevent the whitespace issues noted in prior feedback. The tone should feel confident and efficient, with a product-led story supported by testimonials, integration credibility, and a clearly visible pricing/cart moment.
